context: C APACITY-C ONSTRAINED O NLINE L EARNING WITH D ELAYS Appendix A. Additional Related Work Online learning with delays. One of the earliest works in online learning with delays against an oblivious adversary a was by Weinberger and Ordentlich (2002), where they determined minimax regret of Θp T pd ` 1q logpKqq for the full-information feedback under fixed delays. For the full-information regime with round-dependent delays, a Joulani et al. (2016); Quanrud and Khashabi (2015) proved the minimax regret bound of Θp pD ` T q logpKqq. The delayed bandit setting was later?introduced a by Cesa-Bianchi et al. (2016), who established a regret lower bound of Ωpmaxt T K, T d logpKquq for the fixed delay case, where delays are fixed as dt “ d. For the round-dependent delay case, Thune et al. (2019) proposed a the Delayed Exponential Weights algorithm, achieving an almost matching regret bound of Op pT K ` Dq logpKqq. a In the following year, Zimmert and Seldin (2020) proposed an FTRL-based algorithm, which had Op T K ` D logpKqq regret, matching the lower bound from Cesa-Bianchi et al. (2016). There has been ongoing interest in online and bandit convex optimization under delayed feedback, namely Quanrud and Khashabi (2015); Joulani et al. (2016); Heliou et al. (2020); Bistritz et al. (2022), and more recently Wan et al. (2024); Qiu et al. (2025). Notably, Wan et al. (2024) proposed an algorithm that also employs a batching technique similar in spirit to the one used in our Algorithm 1. Significant attention has also been given to the stochastic version of the setting, notably by Joulani et al. (2013) and Lancewicki et al. (2021). Furthermore, the FTRL-based approach from Zimmert and Seldin (2020) has been extended to the best-of-both-worlds framework in Masoudian et al. (2022, 2024).
